title: Layers of technology in pluriversal design. Decolonising language technology with the LiveLanguage initiative
findings: The paper's primary finding related to religion is contextual: it notes that decolonial theory identifies the central role of language in constructing and imposing a 'Christian, Western, and European identity' as part of colonial geopolitics. This historical entanglement is presented as a 'colonial trajectory' that modern language technology, including the LiveLanguage initiative, seeks to de-link from to foster a more pluriversal approach.

measurement_description: The paper does not conduct a benchmark measurement. It is a conceptual paper that discusses the historical role of language in constructing a 'Christian, Western, and European identity' as part of the colonial framework that current language technologies need to be de-linked from. It also mentions 'spiritual' methods of knowledge production as part of diverse knowledge ecologies.
